name: Jim Costa

items.text: In 1986, Sacramento police reported that Costa, then a state Assemblyman, and a 19-year-old prostitute approached a woman and allegedly agreed to pay her $50. Costa pleaded no contest to soliciting prostitution. He apologized at the time, saying he accepted "full responsibility for my error in judgment."
items.why: This is a 40-year-old personal misdemeanor with no finding of abuse of office or self-dealing, so it has no clear bearing on any criterion, including real work and not taking advantage of the position.

for_review: I couldn't open the 1986 originals: the LA Times 'Assemblyman in Prostitute Incident Issues Apology' (Sept 5, 1986), the AP stories, or the Fresno Bee 'Costa gets probation for soliciting' (Sept 17, 1986). The no-contest plea comes from NNDB. The apology quote and the police account come from a conservative advocacy site (Conservative Institute) that is quoting the earlier coverage. The probation term, the $160 fine and the exact arrest date (Aug 29) appear only on Wikipedia, so I left them out of the text. That site also says police reported a state-leased car was used. If that is confirmed in the 1986 records, it could bear on use of state resources, so check it. Separately, a May 2026 NOTUS report (read via The Washington Sun) says the House Ethics Committee and the Office of Congressional Conduct dismissed a 2023 complaint about alleged advances toward interns. Costa's office says it cooperated and the matter was dismissed. That is a different matter, it was dismissed, and I did not add it as an item. One search on the owner's named sites (Alex Jones/Infowars, Stew Peters, Ryan Dawson) turned up nothing relevant to Costa. Attendance was not weighed, as instructed.
